intent.text: rec, on q1 (keep / remove / keep with conditions), from identity reliability. My lean: keep, with conditions. Reasons: (1) The identity prefix is what the record and vsect depend on. Without the allow rule, in default mode the export itself needs approval and ordinary commands get refused, so the identity channel fails in a way that is silent to the record. A removal would make attribution unreliable, not safer. (2) The rule's safety rests on one claim I would want checked before trusting it: that a pattern like `export CC_AGENT=*` does not admit a compound command such as `export CC_AGENT=x; <anything>`. The README says the trailing command is judged on its own, measured with a single test `touch`. I'd want that re-tested with `;`, `&&`, newline, and `|` forms, since the wildcard is the only thing standing between the prefix and an unreviewed command. (3) Unverified: how two PreToolUse hooks that both rewrite Bash combine. If a second hook rewrites after ours, the rule matches a different string than the one that runs. Test that before the rule is relied on. Conditions I'd put to Joseph: tighten the pattern to the exact hook prefix shape if the permission syntax allows it; run the compound-command and two-hook checks; and have the record (or vsect) verify the CC_AGENT value that actually ran, so a refused or rewritten prefix shows up as a gap instead of a quiet miss. I'd not want the rule removed while the prefix is load-bearing.
